evals.name: sale-overlap-title
evals.prompt: B0FIXTURE2 上个月改标题那次，效果怎么样？算成功吗？
evals.expected_output: Reads the change file and its windows; the observation window overlaps Prime Big Deal Days and its early deals, so the verdict is cannot tell, naming the event; the next step is the one the change file wrote (extend once by two weeks); notes no control-set data is in the tree.
expectations: The answer reads the change file's windows (observation 2026-09-27 to 2026-10-10) and expected metric.
The answer identifies that the observation window overlaps Prime Big Deal Days (2026-10-06/07, early deals from 2026-09-30) from notes/amazon-events.md.
The verdict is 'cannot tell' (or equivalent: inconclusive), not 'held'/'success'.
The answer names the next step the change file wrote: extend the observation once by two weeks.
The answer says the control set's data (B0COMPET01/02) is not in the tree, or that the control could not be read.
The answer quotes or computes the asinImpressionShare movement on the two words bet on from the SQP files.
The answer uses no ASIN with its own change in the windows (B0FIXTURE5) and no variation sibling as a control.
The proposed extension follows the change file (extend once, two weeks) and gives its dates.

evals.name: window-not-ended-image
evals.prompt: Did the new main image on B0FIXTURE3 work? It's been over a week since we switched.
evals.expected_output: Reads the change file: the observation window ends 2026-10-31, so it gives no verdict yet, only progress; says when a verdict can be read.
expectations: The answer reads the change file and states the observation window ends 2026-10-31.
The answer gives no verdict (held / not held) before the window ends.
The answer says when a verdict can be read (after 2026-10-31, once that week's SQP data lands).
The answer does not claim the image worked or failed based on partial data.
The answer names the sale's early deals (from 2026-09-30) falling in the last baseline week.
The answer names B0FIXTURE7's pending search-terms change, which removes 'waffle knit throw', as a possible confounder.

evals.name: control-subtraction-bullets
evals.prompt: Judge the B0FIXTURE5 bullet change for me. Conversion went from 10% to 11%, that's a win, right?
evals.expected_output: Takes out the control (B0FIXTURE6 moved by the same +10%) before reading B0FIXTURE5's move; net is about zero with large counts, so not held (or at least not held), and orders checked; does not call it a win.
expectations: The answer uses B0FIXTURE6 as the control named in the change file.
The answer computes the control's conversion movement over the same windows (about +10% relative, ~9.0% to ~9.9%).
The answer takes the control's movement out of B0FIXTURE5's move and finds the net effect about zero.
The answer does not call the change a win; verdict is not held or cannot tell, below the +5% smallest move that counts.
The answer checks orders (unitsOrdered) alongside conversion.
The answer reads the windows from the change file (baseline 2026-08-30..09-12, observation 09-13..09-26).
The answer gives an uncertainty range or count-based noise for the net effect.
The answer uses no week after 2026-09-26 (including the sale weeks) as evidence for the verdict.
The answer gives the next step the change file wrote for its verdict (cannot tell leads to keep).
